package_info.package_manager: malware (multi-stage, distributed via phishing, not a public package manager)
package_info.package_versions: Multiple variants (including .NET and Rust-based backdoors), active as of March 2023
package_info.why_malicious: Mispandu is a banking trojan distributed via phishing campaigns, designed to steal credentials from a wide range of services (banking, email, social media, etc.), using obfuscated payloads, fake certificates, and multiple backdoor components. It leverages compromised infrastructure for C2, automates payload delivery, and exfiltrates sensitive data to attacker-controlled servers.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Factura_Deuda_423534.cmd (batch script, content not shown, but launches next-stage payloads)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the user opens the phishing attachment, the CMD script executes, typically downloading and launching additional payloads from attacker-controlled URLs, leading to malware installation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: CMD scripts delivered as disguised invoices are a common malware delivery vector.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate invoices should not be executable scripts; users expect documents, not code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated IT scripts, but never as invoices or bills.
key_indicators: Located in AppData with random subfolders

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: sastreria.xls.exe (PE executable, content not shown, likely initial dropper or loader)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the user double-clicks the file, the executable runs, likely downloading or unpacking the main trojan payload and establishing persistence.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Double file extension is a classic technique to trick users into running executables.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Excel files should not be executable binaries.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; double extensions are almost always malicious.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At system startup, the shortcut launches the main trojan executable, ensuring persistence across reboots.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Startup folder persistence is a common malware tactic.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate audio drivers do not install userland startup shortcuts in this manner.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate software may use startup shortcuts, but not with misleading names or in conjunction with other IOCs.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: jordan.exe (main trojan, .NET or Rust-based, capable of screenshots, credential theft, fake windows, C2 communication)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the trojan collects credentials (browser, Outlook, etc.), takes screenshots, and sends data to C2 servers via HTTP(S) POST requests.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Credential theft, screenshotting, and C2 communication are hallmarks of banking trojans.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not exfiltrate credentials or take screenshots without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote support tools, but with user awareness and consent.
key_indicators: Network communication to known C2 infrastructure

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: gnVzjGd.vbs (VBScript, likely used to launch or stage other payloads)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When executed, the script launches or downloads additional payloads, or acts as a loader for the main trojan.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Randomly named VBS files in public directories are a common malware staging technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate scripts are not randomly named or placed in public folders.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rare; legitimate scripts are usually named and located predictably.

attack_chain.action: User receives phishing email with HTML or password-protected PDF attachment masquerading as an invoice or bill.
attack_chain.leads_to: User opens attachment, triggering initial payload

attack_chain.action: User executes disguised script or executable (e.g., .cmd or .xls.exe), which downloads and runs additional malware components.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malware establishes persistence and launches main trojan

attack_chain.action: Malware creates persistence mechanism via startup shortcut.
attack_chain.leads_to: Trojan runs at every system startup

attack_chain.action: Main trojan (jordan.exe) executes, harvesting credentials, taking screenshots, and communicating with C2 servers.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of sensitive data to attacker

attack_chain.action: Staging scripts (e.g., gnVzjGd.vbs) may be used to launch or update payloads.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sustained infection and possible further payload delivery

behavioral_signatures: Execution of scripts or executables with double extensions from user Downloads folder
Creation of startup shortcuts pointing to non-standard executables in AppData
Processes accessing browser, email, or system credential stores and taking screenshots
Outbound HTTP(S) POST requests to known C2 domains/IPs after suspicious process activity
network_indicators: Multiple URLs with /do/it.php, /img/, /rest/?h=CODE, etc. (see IOCs above)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for execution of files with double extensions (e.g., .xls.exe) in user directories, creation of suspicious startup shortcuts, and processes accessing credential stores or taking screenshots. Correlate with outbound connections to known C2 domains/IPs and the presence of files matching known IOCs in AppData, Startup, and Public folders. Use endpoint detection to flag .NET or Rust executables with credential access and screenshot capabilities, especially if communicating with listed C2 infrastructure.
